rationale: itnet-claude-agentic: pretrain_epochs=120, pretrain_lr=0.001, itnet_k=1, itnet_alpha=0.0, unet_c=16, finetune_epochs=0, finetune_lr=0.0001, train_n=400, val_n=200, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, rationale=iter-5 (breast ItNet v1). SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: iter-3 (k1,alpha0.1) hr 0.8199; iter-4 (k1,alpha0.05) hr 0.8666 (+0.047 from HALVING alpha). Clear monotone: LESS DC step = HIGHER hr. (2) FAILURE MODE: the fixed untrained DC step (x <- x_denoised - alpha*FBP(R*x_denoised - g)) re-injects sparse-view streaks; every alpha reduction has helped -> the DC step is NET-HARMFUL on 128-view breast. (3) ONE KNOB: itnet_alpha 0.05 -> 0.0 (all else = iter-4). At alpha=0 the DC step contributes exactly zero, so recon == pure pretrained-denoiser output -> this is the DECISIVE test of the DC step net effect. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if I zero the DC step, hr rises above 0.8666 because the fixed DC step has only hurt so far; the pure denoiser is the ceiling for this pretrain-then-fixed-DC architecture. FALSIFIER: if hr drops vs iter-4, a small DC step IS mildly helpful and the optimum alpha is ~0.05 (interior) -> future iters tune the DENOISER (data/width/epochs), not alpha. (5) BUDGET: compute-free change (float), ~1190s = in budget. (6) Loop continues to iter-20.
